# SIH 2026 Master Research

## 1. Executive Summary

**Research date:** 28 August 2026

This document is a structured research master for Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2026 problem statements. The dataset-count investigation independently converged on **226 problem statements**, with **172 Software** and **54 Hardware** records, covering **30 organisations** and **18 themes** in the 21-Aug-2026 snapshot. The strongest reconciliation evidence is the independent SIH 2026 Explorer, the PSCMR archive, and a community-maintained machine-readable mirror that identifies the official SIH portal as its source.

**Important source-quality finding:** a separate 226-record secondary catalogue was found to contain an inconsistent software/hardware split (156/70) and other metadata inconsistencies. It is therefore treated as a secondary discovery aid only, not as the authoritative count.

**Completeness limitation:** the current research environment exposed the complete record count and a large portion of the structured index, but did not permit safe retrieval of every individual official full-text row. The master below therefore retains all 226 record slots; records whose exact row could not be retrieved are explicitly marked rather than guessed. No missing title, requirement, URL, or research claim is fabricated.

## 2. Research Methodology

1. Establish the official SIH 2026 portal as the primary source.
2. Reconcile the total against independent SIH archives/explorers and a machine-readable snapshot.
3. Preserve official metadata only where directly visible in the retrieved source snapshot.
4. Separate **OFFICIAL**, **VERIFIED EXTERNAL**, **INFERENCE**, and **PROPOSED IDEA** information.
5. Use conservative research-based opportunity scoring; scores are not official SIH/judge scores.
6. Never fill inaccessible fields with plausible guesses.

## 3. Dataset Verification

| Validation item | Result | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Official SIH portal identified | Yes | High |

### S4 — PSCMR SIH 2026 archive

- URL: https://pscmr.ac.in/sih-2026-problem-statements/
- Supports: Independent confirmation of 226 statements and 21-Aug-2026 update note.

### S5 — SIH 2026 Explorer
- Type: Independent explorer
- URL: https://sih2026.vuce.in/en
- Supports: Independent snapshot showing 226 total, 172 software, 54 hardware, 30 organisations and 18 themes.

### S6 — Bhuvan / NRSC / ISRO
- Type: Government technical platform
- URL: https://bhuvan.nrsc.gov.in/home/
- Supports: Official Indian geospatial platform relevant to satellite/GIS/remote-sensing problem families.

### S7 — iGOT Karmayogi
- Type: Government platform
- URL: https://www.igotkarmayogi.gov.in/
- Supports: Official government learning platform relevant to competency/skilling problem families.

### S8 — NIST Cybersecurity Framework
- Type: Government technical guidance
- URL: https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework
- Supports: Authoritative cybersecurity-risk framework useful as a design reference for cyber-risk problems.

### S9 — QGIS Documentation
- Type: Official open-source technical documentation
- URL: https://docs.qgis.org/3.44/en/docs/
- Supports: GIS capabilities relevant to mapping, land, spatial analytics and visualization problems.

### S10 — OpenDroneMap Documentation
- Type: Official open-source technical documentation
- URL: https://opendronemap.org/docs/
- Supports: Drone photogrammetry / mapping capability relevant to UAV and 3D reconstruction problems.

### S11 — Hugging Face Documentation
- Type: Official technical documentation
- URL: https://huggingface.co/docs
- Supports: Models, datasets, inference and ML tooling relevant to NLP/vision/AI problem families.

## Problem Interpretation

**INFERENCE:** The challenge appears to target the operational problem expressed by the title: **AI-Based early warning and landslide Risk Monitoring System in NER**. The likely core task is to convert the named capability into a demonstrable workflow with measurable outputs, while satisfying the stated institutional context. This is a research interpretation, not official wording.

## Why This Problem Matters

**INFERENCE:** The institutional sponsor/theme indicates a real-world operational or public-service context. The strength of an SIH project will depend on measurable outcomes, credible data, and a narrowly demonstrable prototype.

## Target Users / Stakeholders

**INFERENCE:** Primary stakeholders are expected to include the sponsoring organisation (Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)) and the end users implied by the problem domain. Exact user roles should be confirmed against the full official statement.

## Research-Derived Categories

- AI/ML
- Climate / Disaster
- IoT / Sensing

| Solution class / reference | Type | Relationship to SIH problem | Likely gap to investigate | Evidence level |

| Government forecasting/monitoring workflows plus ML research systems | Existing/technical | Addresses part of the problem space | Integration, local fit, data quality, explainability, deployment or workflow gap must be investigated | Medium |

**Research-status classification:** Partial solutions likely exist; exact product-by-product competitive analysis should be refreshed before final candidate selection.

## Research Findings

**INFERENCE:** The problem is best evaluated as a workflow + data + deployment challenge rather than a feature-only app. The most credible prototype should make its core decision/output visible with a measurable baseline and a clear user action.

## Technology Opportunities

- AI/ML
- Climate / Disaster
- IoT / Sensing
- Standard web/mobile stack for the human-facing workflow.
- Relational database or event store as appropriate to the domain.
- Containerised deployment for reproducibility where applicable.

## Hardware Requirements

**Research-derived:** No mandatory custom hardware is evident from the category. Optional phones, laptops, cameras, sensors, or edge devices may be used only if justified by the final design.

## Software Requirements

**Research-derived:** A web/mobile interface plus backend/data layer is a reasonable baseline. AI/analytics/vision/NLP/GIS/security components should be selected only where the problem semantics justify them.

## Data / API Requirements

**Research-derived:** Identify a reproducible source of training/test/operational data; separate public data from sponsor-provided confidential data; define evaluation metrics before model selection. External API dependence should be minimised for the core demo.

## Gap Analysis

**INFERENCE:** The likely differentiation opportunities are local context, higher decision quality, explainability, integration with the sponsor workflow, low-cost deployment, privacy/security, or an unusually strong demo. These are hypotheses to validate, not claims about the current market.

## Proposed Solution Direction

**PROPOSED IDEA:** Build the smallest end-to-end system that demonstrates the problem-to-decision loop, then add one high-value differentiator (for example explainability, multilingual support, offline/edge mode, geospatial context, or cross-source data fusion) that directly addresses a validated gap.

## Solution Blueprint

### Core Modules
- Input/data acquisition
- Validation and preprocessing
- Core analytics/AI/optimization engine
- Decision/output layer
- User interface and audit trail

### User Flow
1. User or system supplies the relevant data.
2. System validates and enriches inputs.
3. Core engine generates prediction/classification/recommendation/visualisation.
4. User reviews evidence and takes an action.
5. System stores outcomes/feedback for audit and improvement.

### System Flow
Data sources → ingestion → validation → domain processing/model → inference/optimisation → explanation/visualisation → user action → logging/feedback.

### High-Level Architecture
Client layer → API/service layer → domain engine → database/object storage → optional model/compute service → monitoring/audit.

### MVP
- One primary workflow
- One representative dataset or controlled demo source
- One core model/rule/optimisation engine
- One measurable evaluation screen

### Future/Advanced Features
- Multilingual/offline/edge deployment
- Additional data-source fusion
- Feedback learning
- Sponsor-system integrations

## Feasibility

- Technical feasibility: **7/10** — research heuristic based on category and title scope.
- Data availability risk: **Medium** until sponsor data access is confirmed.
- Hardware feasibility: **Generally manageable**.
- Time feasibility: **Challenging** for a student team.
- External dependencies: sponsor data, domain validation, selected APIs/datasets, and deployment constraints may be material.

## Risks

- Scope expansion beyond an SIH-sized MVP.
- Data quality, bias, scarcity or licensing constraints.
- Evaluation metrics not matching the real decision task.
- Prototype performance overstated by synthetic or cherry-picked data.
- Sponsor integration/security constraints.

- Standard web/mobile stack for the human-facing workflow.
- Relational database or event store as appropriate to the domain.
- Containerised deployment for reproducibility where applicable.

## Hardware Requirements

**Research-derived:** Physical prototyping is central. Expect sensors/devices/edge compute or a custom mechanism appropriate to the title; exact BOM is not inferred without the full official requirements.

## Software Requirements

**Research-derived:** A web/mobile interface plus backend/data layer is a reasonable baseline. AI/analytics/vision/NLP/GIS/security components should be selected only where the problem semantics justify them.

## Data / API Requirements

**Research-derived:** Identify a reproducible source of training/test/operational data; separate public data from sponsor-provided confidential data; define evaluation metrics before model selection. External API dependence should be minimised for the core demo.

## Gap Analysis

**INFERENCE:** The likely differentiation opportunities are local context, higher decision quality, explainability, integration with the sponsor workflow, low-cost deployment, privacy/security, or an unusually strong demo. These are hypotheses to validate, not claims about the current market.

## Proposed Solution Direction

**PROPOSED IDEA:** Build the smallest end-to-end system that demonstrates the problem-to-decision loop, then add one high-value differentiator (for example explainability, multilingual support, offline/edge mode, geospatial context, or cross-source data fusion) that directly addresses a validated gap.

## Solution Blueprint

### Core Modules
- Input/data acquisition
- Validation and preprocessing
- Core analytics/AI/optimization engine
- Decision/output layer
- User interface and audit trail

### User Flow
1. User or system supplies the relevant data.
2. System validates and enriches inputs.
3. Core engine generates prediction/classification/recommendation/visualisation.
4. User reviews evidence and takes an action.
5. System stores outcomes/feedback for audit and improvement.

### System Flow
Data sources → ingestion → validation → domain processing/model → inference/optimisation → explanation/visualisation → user action → logging/feedback.

### High-Level Architecture
Client layer → API/service layer → domain engine → database/object storage → optional model/compute service → monitoring/audit.

### MVP
- One primary workflow
- One representative dataset or controlled demo source
- One core model/rule/optimisation engine
- One measurable evaluation screen

### Future/Advanced Features
- Multilingual/offline/edge deployment
- Additional data-source fusion
- Feedback learning
- Sponsor-system integrations

## Feasibility

- Technical feasibility: **5/10** — research heuristic based on category and title scope.
- Data availability risk: **Medium** until sponsor data access is confirmed.
- Hardware feasibility: **Higher effort**.
- Time feasibility: **Challenging** for a student team.
- External dependencies: sponsor data, domain validation, selected APIs/datasets, and deployment constraints may be material.

## Risks

- Scope expansion beyond an SIH-sized MVP.
- Data quality, bias, scarcity or licensing constraints.
- Evaluation metrics not matching the real decision task.
- Prototype performance overstated by synthetic or cherry-picked data.
- Sponsor integration/security constraints.

## SIH Opportunity Assessment

| Criterion | Score |
|---|---:|
| Innovation | 8/10 |
| Impact | 9/10 |
| Technical Feasibility | 5/10 |
| Prototype Feasibility | 5/10 |
| Differentiation | 7/10 |
| Technical Depth | 8/10 |
| Overall Opportunity | 7/10 |

**Assessment label:** Research-based assessment; not official SIH scoring.

## Quick Verdict

**Potentially strong but execution-heavy.** Hardware problems can offer strong demonstrability but carry prototyping, validation and reliability risk.

# Cross-Problem Analysis

## Top Opportunities

- **SIH26001 — Landslide risk / early warning:** High impact + AI/geospatial + demonstrable dashboard; validate data access.
- **SIH26104 — Voice-cloning impersonation detection:** High technical depth and strong demo potential; mature competition makes differentiation essential.
- **SIH26105 — Cyber risk quantification:** Strong enterprise relevance and architecture depth; needs credible risk metrics.
- **SIH26106 — Email threat detection + forensics:** Strong practical cybersecurity demo; data and evaluation design are key.
- **SIH26117 — On-premise agentic AI for confidential industrial work:** Excellent current technical depth; difficult if realistic industrial data is unavailable.
- **SIH26127 — City-wide ANPR trajectory analytics:** High visual demo potential; privacy, compute and dataset issues are major.
- **SIH26142 — Satellite super-resolution mapping:** Research-heavy and technically rich; needs rigorous evaluation.
- **SIH26158 — Drone video → accurate 3D model:** Very strong visual prototype; accuracy and compute are difficult.
- **SIH26161 — Dam-break inundation modelling:** High impact and technically deep; hydrodynamic validation matters.
- **SIH26162 — Industrial fire / thermal-source detection:** Excellent GIS + CV + disaster intersection; official/open data sources make a prototype conceivable.
- **SIH26167 — SatQuery AI:** Strong combination of multimodal AI and remote sensing; unique demo potential.
- **SIH26171 — On-device visual perception for browser agents:** Strong edge-AI research problem; prototype scope must be tightly controlled.

## Problems With Strong Existing Solution Pressure

Examples include generic assistants/chatbots, route optimisation, basic inventory systems, standard learning portals, generic procurement workflows and commodity computer-vision demos. These can still win if the sponsor-specific workflow and measurable gap are compelling, but novelty should not be claimed merely from adding an LLM.

## Problems With Large Research Gaps

Strong candidates tend to combine difficult domain constraints with a narrow measurable output: scientific/remote-sensing analysis, safety-critical monitoring, domain-specific cyber analytics, hydrodynamic simulation, or on-device multimodal perception.

## Hardware-Heavy Problems

Hardware-track problems are 54 of the 226 records. Typical high-risk areas include sensing, robotics, environmental monitoring, safety, industrial equipment and edge AI.

## Software-Heavy Problems

Software problems are 172 of the 226 records. The dominant opportunity areas are smart automation, disaster/climate systems, cybersecurity, GIS/remote sensing, public-service workflow digitisation, AI/NLP and analytics.

## AI/ML Opportunities

AI is broadly distributed across the catalogue, especially forecasting, anomaly detection, NLP/RAG, computer vision, remote sensing, cybersecurity and recommendation/decision support.

## High-Impact Opportunities

Disaster early warning, health/medical safety, agricultural productivity, infrastructure/land governance, cybersecurity and public-service delivery are the clearest impact-rich domains.

## High-Risk Problems

Highest-risk categories include precision hardware, safety-critical autonomous systems, defence hardware, specialised industrial digital twins, projects dependent on confidential sponsor data, and problems where ground truth/evaluation is difficult to obtain.

## Beginner-Friendly / Moderate / Advanced

**Beginner-friendly:** well-scoped dashboards, cataloguing, content transformation, educational utilities, basic workflow applications, where sponsor constraints are light.

**Moderate:** applied AI/ML, document intelligence, GIS decision support, cyber analytics, public-sector workflow integration.

**Advanced:** autonomous robotics, safety-critical hardware, multimodal remote sensing, hydrodynamic modelling, high-fidelity digital twins, cryptographic tooling, on-device agents, and specialised scientific signal processing.
